stage1.impression: Two identical red speakers glow like neon signs in a dark, empty box. Behind them is a tiled back wall with a blotchy camouflage overlay and flat black panels, light cones from the spots streak through the haze above, a stray teal patch sits on an otherwise featureless floor, and nothing in the frame says anyone lives here. At 1:1 the oak plinths are the only surface that reads as a real material; the wall looks like a tiled game texture and the denoiser has softened everything. A design magazine would not publish this as a specific place: it reads as a generic, stage-lit showroom for two speakers, not a listening room.

blocking_9: The bottle-green zone the frame is for (velvet tub chairs, green wool carpet, limewashed walls, hex oak tables with smoked Orb lamps) is not in the frame at all; the floor reads neutral grey (RGB 13/14/12, dE2000 18 from bottle green #1F3A2B).
No sign of life or human scale in the listening zone: no chair backs, no glass, no record, no Orb's warm pool in the foreground.
The speaker cabinets read as glowing neon signs (cabinet face p95 about 170, with clip_pct 0.58 in the speaker region) rather than lit tinted acrylic with clean edges and visible white batts.
The end-grain block lining reads as a square tile grid with a large camouflage overlay, not as end-grain oak blocks at real scale.
The volumetric cones above each speaker read as stage or nightclub light.
Denoiser smear and softness across the wall and floor; no material grain at 1:1.

defects.what: The floor is a near-black, featureless plane (lum_median 15.5, lum_range 37), with no carpet texture, no green and no furniture: the empty foreground of a showroom.
A teal-green patch of light on the floor (RGB 22/35/28) that reads as a stray coloured light or a texture error, not a green carpet.
A dark green-teal object cut off at the right edge, unreadable (lum 13).
The end-grain wall reads as a 10 cm square tile grid with a large-scale blotchy camouflage overlay: it looks procedural, and the overlay is at the wrong scale.
The felt panels behind the speakers are flat black rectangles with no texture or edge definition.
The felt panels behind the speakers are flat black rectangles with no texture or edge definition.
A visible haze cone from the altar spot: stage-light look.
A visible haze cone from the altar spot: stage-light look.
The speaker cabinet glows hot pink as a uniform neon (p95 about 170, clipping 0.58%): the acrylic's edges and depth are lost and it reads as a sign.
The horn is under-lit and murky (lum_median 16): its resin form and its reflections are lost.
Two identical speakers dominate symmetrically: it reads as a product line-up rather than a room.
The left timber return is a flat panel with a uniform repeating grain; no checks, no end grain, no wear.
Denoiser smear throughout: soft, waxy surfaces and no fine grain at 1:1.

changes.problem: The frame is meant to show the bottle-green listening zone facing the altar, but the camera is pressed against the altar and crops out every seat, table, Orb lamp and the carpet.

evidence.measured: The bottom quarter is an empty grey floor (RGB 13/14/12, dE2000 18.1 against #1F3A2B); no chairs or tables are visible.

change.to: pull back to about [10.8, 1.2, 1.15] (seated eye height, behind the rear row of tub chairs), aim at [16.6, 3.0, 1.0], 28-32 mm, f/2.8 focused at about 3.5 m on the nearest Orb table, so two or three velvet chair backs and an Orb on its hex table fill the lower third and the altar sits in the upper middle

changes.expected: The green chairs and carpet occupy 30-40% of the frame, the speakers drop to about a third of the frame height, and the image reads as a room you sit in.

changes.problem: The listening zone has no light pools of its own; with the camera pulled back, the green chairs and carpet will crush unless the Orbs and downlights lift them.

evidence.measured: lum_median 13.2, lum_p95 23: the foreground floor is near-black.

change.setting: each Orb W and glow; the Domes' downlights
change.to: Orb 10-12 W, glow 1.4, so each table carries a warm 2400 K pool on the velvet and carpet; keep the downlights at 260 W, or trim them to 220 W if the Domes' pools at the counter compete

changes.expected: Warm pools on each table and chair arm, with dark green between them; foreground median 22-35.

changes.problem: The speaker cabinets glow like neon signs instead of reading as lit tinted acrylic with polished edges.

evidence.measured: Speaker region lum_p95 170, clip_pct 0.58; the face is flat hot pink.

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area
change.to: 1.0-1.2 W/m2, 2700 K; move the altar spots so more of their light grazes the cabinet sides and the edges glow, rather than lighting the cabinets from inside

changes.expected: The cabinet face reads as deep red tinted acrylic, with the white batts visible as a soft lighter mass and the edge bevels bright; the highlights hold below clipping.

changes.problem: The resin horns sit in murk; the most sculptural part of the speaker is lost.

change.to: 110 W, 2500 K, cone 24 deg, re-aimed 25-30 cm higher, onto the horns' upper flare

changes.expected: The horns show their form and a clean specular line; horn median 30-50.

changes.problem: Visible light cones in the haze above each speaker read as stage or nightclub light.

evidence.measured: Distinct bright shafts above both speakers, with hard sides.

changes.expected: Atmosphere is felt as a faint lift in the shadows, with no visible beams.

changes.problem: The end-grain block lining reads as a procedural tile grid with a camouflage overlay, not as oak end grain.

evidence.measured: A regular square grid with large blotches spanning 4-8 blocks; lum_range 24.5, with no growth rings visible at 3x.

change.setting: the oak's stain / the end-grain material finish
change.from: large-scale tonal blotches over a uniform block texture
change.to: per-block random tone (plus or minus 12% value, slight hue shift), visible growth rings and checks in each block, a slight random height variation and a matte, oiled sheen; remove the large-scale noise overlay

changes.expected: The wall reads as hand-laid end-grain blocks at real scale, catching the altar light unevenly.

changes.problem: No sign of life in the listening zone.

evidence.measured: No props in the foreground or on any surface near the altar.

change.from: props at the counter only (glasses, coupe, record, coat)
change.to: a half-drunk rocks glass and a record sleeve on the nearest Orb table, a jacket over one tub chair's back, a sleeve leaning against an altar plinth

changes.expected: Human scale and a story in the foreground, without clutter.

changes.problem: The denoiser smear leaves every surface waxy, with no fine grain at 1:1.

evidence.measured: The timber panel and the wall show smoothed, blurred grain; the proof is at scale 0.3.

change.to: 512 samples, adaptive 0.01, denoise with albedo and normal passes at full 2400 x 1600, then add a fine 0.5% film grain in post

changes.expected: Velvet pile, carpet and timber grain survive at 1:1; no blotches in the dark areas.

out_of_scope.request: Show one speaker rather than a symmetric pair, so the frame stops reading as a product line-up.
out_of_scope.why: The Ember pair on the altar is fixed by the card; reframing (c1) mitigates the line-up effect instead.

out_of_scope.request: Give the felt panels behind the speakers a visible texture and a lighter tone, so they stop reading as black voids.
out_of_scope.why: The felt is part of the room's fixed design; only its lighting may change, and c4/c2 may lift it slightly.
